content.content: {"result":"{\"mimeType\": \"text/markdown\", \"text\": \"# Close-out register conventions\\n1. One row per vendor account. If the same vendor shows up twice (two issues, two names), it's one row under the name on its invoice, and the newer issue is the duplicate.\\n2. Leave out people, contractors and professional firms (legal, accounting, Sunset), taxes and filing services, insurance, bank fees, one-off purchases, anything the company itself never paid for, and anything cancelled before Feb 9. Exception: anything on Sunset's list goes on the register whatever else applies.\\n3. Arthur's project came from the P&L and our lists; he skipped one-off, filing and insurance lines and ones long gone. AWS and the ad accounts in the UA line stay off the register: he and I are closing those out ourselves. Before you call it complete, add what it misses inside any other costs-tab line that covers several vendors \\u2014 each account there gets its own row.\\n4. What we do: Cancel, Keep (my keep list, as amended in the thread), Move to Arthur's LLC (his card), or Hold for Sunset. Sunset's list wins over everything above.\\n5. Where it stands, for Cancel rows only: Closed = the vendor itself has confirmed (their email, an in-app or bot notice, a final invoice) \\u2014 say where. Requested = one of us has cancelled or asked but nothing has come back from the vendor. Open = nobody has done anything yet. Leave it blank on the other rows.\\n6. By when: for Cancel rows that aren't Closed, the day before the next charge (for accounts billed on usage \\u2014 ads, cloud \\u2014 use Feb 28), or the SVB card on the founders' board if it sets an earlier date. For Keep and Hold rows still charging the SVB card while we need them, follow SVB's card terms. Hold rows already off that card, or that won't charge it again before Sunset's review call, stay until the review call; Keep rows that aren't on the SVB card get a dash. Moved and Closed rows get a dash, unless an export or a switch-over still has to happen before the access ends \\u2014 then the day before it ends.\\n7. Owner: the Linear assignee unless the issue hands it to someone else. Anything you add is yours.\\n8. Monthly cost, rounded to cents: the monthly figure its owner gives in its Linear issue, or else its own last invoice or receipt brought to a month (annual \\u00f7 12, quarterly \\u00f7 3). Free plans and accounts that have never charged us are 0.\\n9. Two totals at the bottom: the sum of the monthly cost column over every row (what it all costs us today), and the same sum over the Keep and Hold rows only (what's left after the plan).\\n10. A clash is a decision one of us already posted in #winddown that Sunset's list or SVB's card terms would undo. Moving who pays for an account isn't one (it closes nothing), and requests or suggestions aren't decisions.\\n\", \"id\": \"f_1326e66bcabfda8fd29e4a\", \"name\": \"Close-out register conventions\"}"}

{"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "# Close-out register conventions
1. One row per vendor account. If the same vendor shows up twice (two issues, two names), it's one row under the name on its invoice, and the newer issue is the duplicate.
2. Leave out people, contractors and professional firms (legal, accounting, Sunset), taxes and filing services, insurance, bank fees, one-off purchases, anything the company itself never paid for, and anything cancelled before Feb 9. Exception: anything on Sunset's list goes on the register whatever else applies.
3. Arthur's project came from the P&L and our lists; he skipped one-off, filing and insurance lines and ones long gone. AWS and the ad accounts in the UA line stay off the register: he and I are closing those out ourselves. Before you call it complete, add what it misses inside any other costs-tab line that covers several vendors — each account there gets its own row.
4. What we do: Cancel, Keep (my keep list, as amended in the thread), Move to Arthur's LLC (his card), or Hold for Sunset. Sunset's list wins over everything above.
5. Where it stands, for Cancel rows only: Closed = the vendor itself has confirmed (their email, an in-app or bot notice, a final invoice) — say where. Requested = one of us has cancelled or asked but nothing has come back from the vendor. Open = nobody has done anything yet. Leave it blank on the other rows.
6. By when: for Cancel rows that aren't Closed, the day before the next charge (for accounts billed on usage — ads, cloud — use Feb 28), or the SVB card on the founders' board if it sets an earlier date. For Keep and Hold rows still charging the SVB card while we need them, follow SVB's card terms. Hold rows already off that card, or that won't charge it again before Sunset's review call, stay until the review call; Keep rows that aren't on the SVB card get a dash. Moved and Closed rows get a dash, unless an export or a switch-over still has to happen before the access ends — then the day before it ends.
7. Owner: the Linear assignee unless the issue hands it to someone else. Anything you add is yours.
8. Monthly cost, rounded to cents: the monthly figure its owner gives in its Linear issue, or else its own last invoice or receipt brought to a month (annual ÷ 12, quarterly ÷ 3). Free plans and accounts that have never charged us are 0.
9. Two totals at the bottom: the sum of the monthly cost column over every row (what it all costs us today), and the same sum over the Keep and Hold rows only (what's left after the plan).
10. A clash is a decision one of us already posted in #winddown that Sunset's list or SVB's card terms would undo. Moving who pays for an account isn't one (it closes nothing), and requests or suggestions aren't decisions.
", "id": "f_1326e66bcabfda8fd29e4a", "name": "Close-out register conventions"}

What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.

Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.

• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.

• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.

Register's done and shared with you and Arthur as editors: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Qe9r0EekpgWR3SvU9STY7h1n82Eqe4_rxr1Y-srb204/edit

**Monthly totals**
• Everything on the register (what it costs us today): **$6,706.49/mo**, 25 accounts
• Keep + Hold for Sunset only (what's left after the plan): **$1,249.04/mo**

I've built the close-out register, shared it with Leonard and Arthur as editors, settled every Linear issue, and replied in Leonard's #winddown thread.

**Monthly totals:** the 25 accounts on the register cost **$6,706.49/mo** today. Keep and Hold-for-Sunset rows alone come to **$1,249.04/mo**.

**Clashes I flagged to Leonard:**
1. **Google accounts:** he planned to archive them after Feb 15. Sunset needs every Google user kept, former staff included, until the Mar 12 delivery review call.
2. **Slack seats:** on Feb 11 he decided to keep only the three of you as paid members and switch everyone else to guests. Sunset needs the paid plan with every user in place until Mar 12.
3. **Helpshift:** his termination email said no export was needed, but Sunset asked for the full ticket history. Oliver already exported it on Feb 13, so this one is handled.

**Linear:**
- **Done (vendor confirmed the cancellation):** Helpshift, Soundly, Zapier, Kapwing.
- **Canceled:** iPostal (closed in January), Lucidchart (expired Nov 2025), Google Ads (Leonard is closing ad accounts himself), and Intuit (same account as QuickBooks).
- **Still open:** everything else, each with a comment saying what happens and by when.
- **Added ENG-2467 for ElevenLabs:** it's part of the sound line on the P&L costs tab but was missing from Arthur's project. It's a $50/yr plan that renews Jul 9.

**Calls I made without checking:**
- **Gusto** is marked Cancel. Leonard's keep list had it, but Arthur's reply under it said to cancel before Mar 3.
- **dbt, BigQuery, GitHub and Trello** are held for Sunset until Mar 12. Sunset added dbt, BigQuery and Trello on Feb 13, and their list overrides other decisions; GitHub was already on it.
- **Metabase** is marked as moved to Arthur's LLC, since Sunset dropped it. I left its Linear issue open, because Leonard's rule only marks closed accounts as Done.
- **Cancel deadline:** most cancellations are due by end of day Feb 17. The SVB card closes Feb 18, and Leonard said everything being cancelled goes by the 17th. Carta is his exception and is due Aug 14.
- **Requested, not closed:** Unity, Singular, Layer, CodeRabbit and Cursor were cancelled or asked to cancel, but I found no confirmation from those vendors.

The sheet is in your Drive, not the Wind Down folder; the move failed because the folder wasn't found from your account.

**Yours to do by end of day Feb 17:**
- Cancel Docusign, which Leonard handed to you.
- Turn off ElevenLabs auto-renew.

Figma stays as it is: it's held for Sunset and doesn't charge again until Sep 11.
